title: Existence of the normalized derived direct-image comparison
statement: For compatible coefficient changes on the pro-etale sites, there exists a natural isomorphism between the derived direct image after restriction along the source coefficient map and restriction along the target coefficient map after derived direct image, satisfying the displayed unit-normalization equation of the parent node for every cochain complex.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, comparison and normalization on K-injective resolutions

proof.text: Transport the source SU- and RU-module categories and the target RV-module category to the AsSmall pro-etale sites using the existing module equivalences. On those small sites construct the identity-topos coefficient restriction and the continuous ringed-topos direct image associated with f and its specified coefficient map. Their module functors identify sectionwise with the original restriction and direct-image functors. Apply the resolution clause of ringedToposDerivedPushforwardComposition: for a K-injective SU-complex I and a K-injective resolution j of its RU-restriction, directImage(j) is a quasi-isomorphism. Exact equivalences preserve K-injectivity and preserve and reflect quasi-isomorphisms, so transport this conclusion back to the original sites.

By naturality of the right-derived unit at j, the unit on the restricted I is invertible: the unit on its K-injective resolution is invertible and both j and directImage(j) become isomorphisms after localization. This is cancellation of isomorphisms in the naturality square; restriction itself is never asserted to preserve K-injectivity.

Take the mate of the termwise descended inverse-image comparison under the two canonical derived adjunctions. The existing derived_mate_factors calculation and the ordinary restrictionPullback_mate calculation give the required normalization on every cochain complex. On K-injective I all the other arrows in that normalization are invertible, including the right-derived unit just proved invertible on the restricted I; hence the mate component is invertible. Every derived object is isomorphic to the localization of a K-injective complex, so naturality makes all components invertible. The resulting natural isomorphism has exactly the displayed normalization.
